results.description:
Willpower is not enough against social media algorithms!

That’s why I made one sec:

one sec adds friction to distracting apps to make them less appealing…long-term!

This principle works really well: we have gained scientific evidence in numerous research studies with the Max-Planck Institute, with the German and Danish government, and in dozens more scientific collaborations:

one sec has incredible effects on your screen time: app usage drops by 57% on average!

…just read our App Store reviews or try it for yourself if you don’t believe me (…you should really try it)!


How is one sec different from Screen Time limits or app blockers?
- one sec DELAYS access to distracting apps instead of blocking apps completely – that’s an important difference psychologically.
- This way, we solve the screen time problem at its roots: long-term & sustainably!
- one sec is always on, and makes using social media just slightly more annoying…so you’ll end up using it only when you actually have a reason!


Which apps can I use with one sec?
- You can set up one sec with any app you’d like to use less / more intentional.
- Most popular use-cases are: social media, games, video streaming, dating, stock/coin trading, adult content.
- Using one sec with one app of your choice if completely free, for more you’ll need to purchase one sec pro (we also need to finance development of our app!).


What if I get stuck scrolling?
- No worries, one sec offers a Doom Scroll Emergency Brake: We call it Re-Intervention.
- After a set time (e.g. 5 minutes) you’ll be kicked out of social media, and you’ll have to go through an intervention again to unlock more time.


Where can I learn more about the scientific background of one sec?
→ https://one-sec.app/research


Can I use one sec to interrupt access to websites as well?
→ Yes, one sec offers a free Safari extension as well.


How does one sec work technically?
- one sec uses Shortcuts Automation to toggle a deep breath animation whenever you open one of the configured apps (Instagram, Twitter, YouTube…).
- This breaks unconscious social media habits short-term (literally, as soon as you have set it up) and even helps long-term by adding more friction when opening these apps.


Integrations:
- Structured: one sec blocks apps during unfinished tasks.
- LENGO: learn vocabulary to unlock social media.


I developed one sec for myself in 2020…and it worked so well I decided to upload it to the App Store.

Especially for people with ADHD one sec is a great tool to gain back control for incredible focus and concentration.

– Frederik

WillStone is an app designed to help you gradually reduce phone usage. Instead of implementing strict daily screen time limits like other digital wellbeing apps, we've designed a unique time exchange system:

Entertainment apps have limited usage time, but you can earn more screen time through focused activities and positive apps (such as learning, exercising, walking, meditation, building habits, early bedtime, etc.).

We help you put down your phone progressively while building healthy habits!

【Design Philosophy】
- Immediate satisfaction drives motivation: A 1898 study by Thorndike showed that behaviors followed by satisfying consequences tend to be repeated, while those leading to unpleasant outcomes are less likely to recur. James Clear's "Atomic Habits" also mentions the four-step habit model—cue, craving, response, and reward.
- Cold turkey approaches are hard to maintain: We've tried many screen control apps like Opal, ClearSpace and Apple Screen Time. Often, these get uninstalled after 3 days—just like quitting any addictive substance, going cold turkey rarely works.
- The key to painlessly building good habits is: balancing desires with personal growth.

【How It Works】
- First, set up two categories of apps:
  - Apps you want to limit, such as Instagram, Twitter, TikTok, shopping apps, etc. We'll call these "entertainment apps."
  - Apps that help you grow, like reading apps, Duolingo, vocabulary builders, etc. After setup, grant WillStone screen time access permissions to begin.
- Initially, you get 10 minutes daily for entertainment apps: Once you exceed this, a full-screen notification appears with no "remind me later" option.
- Want more entertainment time? Use positive apps to earn additional screen time. Read books, learn vocabulary, and you can continue browsing. You can also earn time by walking or exercising.

【Use Cases】
We offer multiple ways to earn time:
- Focus Mode: For exam prep, vacation study, evening reading/drawing—use our offline timer. During focus sessions, only selected apps remain accessible, helping you concentrate. Earn entertainment time as a reward.
- Reading, Vocabulary, Language Learning: Add learning apps to your positive apps list—we'll automatically track usage and reward proportional entertainment time.
- Early Bedtime: WillStone reminds you when it's bedtime and locks entertainment apps. Maintaining healthy sleep patterns earns bonus entertainment minutes the next day, encouraging your brain to embrace better sleep habits.
- Exercise and Walking: WillStone automatically tracks your activity duration (via Apple Health) and rewards entertainment time proportionally. Meditation counts too!
- Daily Habits: Whether it's drinking water, post-work shower, neck exercises, or rehabilitation—customize your habits with reminders and goals. Complete daily tasks to earn entertainment time, making healthy lifestyle changes effortless.

【Features】
- Exchange System: Convert positive app usage, early bedtime, habits, exercise, meditation, walking into entertainment app time
- Custom Exchange Rates: Adjust difficulty levels and conversion ratios for gradual progress
- Widgets: Display available time and quick-start focus timer on home screen
- Analytics: Track your time balance and app usage distribution in "Performance" and "Data" sections

Have other habits you'd like to build? Contact us and let us know!

A schedule-style screen-time manager for parents, installed on your child's iPhone or iPad.

Built-in Screen Time is a blunt tool. RestBud adds five things it can't do:

• Lock schedules — apps you add to a Lock are blocked all day by default; check weekdays and set one or more unlock windows (say, 7:00–12:00 plus 14:00–16:00 on Mon/Wed/Fri) and they open and close automatically.

Screen time apps fail for one simple reason. You can always turn them off, even the strict ones.

Friction is not accountability. Scrollmates does not pretend to be unbreakable. It just makes sure you are not the only one who knows.

Scrollmates gives you and one other person a single shared pool of minutes for the apps you both want to use less. Every minute you spend is a minute they don't get, and the other way round. Nobody is policing anybody. You are drawing from the same account.

HOW A DAY WORKS

You start with a full pool and your blocked apps open normally.

When the pool runs low, your apps are shielded by default, and getting in takes a deliberate claim of up to fifteen minutes at a time.

When the pool is empty, everything on your block list stays shut until your next reset. You can still get in, but it is recorded as a breach and your scrollmate is told.

There is no snooze, and no way to quietly raise your own limit while nobody is looking. The contract is shared, so changing it is something you both see.

HARDCORE MODE

For the days you would rather not have the option. With Hardcore Mode on there is no claiming your way past an empty pool, and no ending the day early.

What remains is a typed emergency of fifteen minutes, and it still goes on the record as a breach. It is not a lock, and we will not pretend otherwise. It is the smallest door we could leave open without lying to you about what any app on your own phone can actually do.

WHAT YOUR SCROLLMATE SEES

Your daily minutes. Your share of the pool. Whether you are scrolling right now.

WHAT THEY NEVER SEE

Which apps you blocked. Anything you did inside them.

That line is deliberate. Accountability does not require surveillance.

BLOCK SCHEDULES

Set the hours that are not up for negotiation. A quiet first hour, a deep work block, a wind-down before bed. Schedules run themselves, and you can each see the other's.

THE JOURNAL

Your week, laid out honestly. How much each of you used, how the split fell, how each day ended, and whether this week beat the last one.

SHARED QUESTS

One level and one streak, shared between you. Keep the day under a ceiling, keep the late nights clear, and you both climb. Break the contract and you both start over. It is the only kind of streak that holds, because neither of you wants to be the one who ended it.

ON YOUR OWN

No scrollmate yet? Solo mode gives you the same pool, the same phases and the same journal. Pair up whenever you're ready.

BEFORE YOU START

Scrollmates uses Apple's Screen Time to shield the apps on your block list. You choose what goes on that list.

results.description:
ScreenFox helps you reduce screen time by caring for a virtual fox whose wellbeing reflects your digital habits. The more mindfully you use distracting apps, the happier your fox becomes. Excessive scrolling makes it sad, and when it runs out of energy, distracting apps stay locked until tomorrow or until you help it recover through focused work.

The Digital Fox Companion:
At the center of ScreenFox is a virtual fox companion that reflects the user’s digital wellbeing.
The fox has hearts that decrease when opening selected apps. Its emotional state changes based on remaining hearts:
- Plenty of hearts: The fox is happy and smiling
- Some hearts: The fox appears neutral
- No hearts: The fox becomes sad and starts crying
When no hearts are left, access to restricted apps is blocked for the rest of the day.

Daily Limits & Reset System:
Users define which apps to manage and set daily hearts.
- Once there are no hearts left, access to selected apps is restricted for the day
- Every unlock of restricted apps consumes a heart to use for a user-defined session length
- At the end of each day, hearts reset to amount of hearts set
This system encourages more intentional and mindful app usage.

Focus Sessions:
Focus sessions help users regain control and restore balance:
- Restricted apps are blocked during focus time
- Completing a focus session restores hearts
- Restored hearts allow additional restricted app unlocks
This creates a positive loop between focus and digital freedom.

Additional Features:
ScreenFox also includes tools to reduce impulsive behavior:
- App launch delay before opening restricted apps
- Session duration limits with reminders during extended usage
These features encourage reflection and break automatic usage patterns.

Motivation System:
To support long-term habit building, the app includes:
- Daily streaks
- Tasks and achievements
- XP and leveling system
Users are rewarded for consistent mindful usage.

User Control:
All restrictions are fully user-defined and can be changed at any time.
ScreenFox is designed to support awareness and self-regulation, not enforce control.

results.description:
Don’t rely on yourself to lock your apps. Let someone else hold your key.

Azukari is an app blocker and screen time limit you share with friends. You lock the apps you choose, such as social media, games, or video. Someone else holds the key, so you cannot quietly undo it.

FRIENDS AND ACCOUNTABILITY PARTNERS
Create a group and pick the apps on your iPhone. Invite a friend or accountability partner, and they hold your key. When you want an app back, ask from your phone. Your friend can approve a timed break, unlock you, or share the key. Use it to study, focus at work, or cut down on scrolling.

Lock until your key holder unlocks you, or for 30 minutes to 4 hours. Lock only the apps you picked, or every app. Key holders confirm with Face ID or their passcode before they unlock you.

STREAKS
Every day with a lock of 30 minutes or more counts toward your streak. Your group sees everyone's streak, so you keep each other going.

SCHEDULES
Set daily lock windows, such as school hours or bedtime. Scheduled windows end on their own. Emergency unlocks are limited.

FAMILY SCREEN TIME
Pick when and what apps your children have locked. A parent chooses the apps on the child’s iPhone and sets the lock times. Kids can ask a parent for the key.

PRICING
Only the person who creates the group subscribes (monthly or yearly). Yearly starts with a 7-day free trial. Everyone they invite joins free.

PRIVACY
Azukari uses Apple’s Screen Time permission to block apps. Your app list stays on this iPhone.
